name: P25J — skip the opening: pressing skip or X must leave the game PLAYABLE

steps.note:
RUN IT WITH:  node tools/shoot.mjs --keep-title --out /tmp/p25j --script scenarios/P25J-skip.json --timeout 300000

THE BUG AS REPORTED: 'at the start of the game, the scene where you talk to Papa — if you press skip or the X button it skips the scene, but then you have to go talk to Papa again.'

WHAT WAS WRONG, and it was not a skip bug. `runList()` returns the instant `R.skipReq` is set — that is what makes skip fast — so a beat's own steps never finish. In B1 that mattered because `flag('ch1.awake')` sits at step 26 of 40, and `blocks: ['ch1.awake']` is how the chapter asks 'has this already happened?'. A player who skipped on the FIRST line never reached step 26, so the beat was still ready, and the chapter opened Papa's scene again. The next walk out of the cottage opened it again. That is the bug, and it was not confined to B1: every one of the twenty-seven beats kept its gate flag in the middle of itself.

THE X BUTTON IS THE SAME KEY. `cutsceneScene.onInput` maps `cancel` AND `menu` to `Story.skip()`, so both buttons are one code path and one fix — and this scenario presses each of them.

THE FIX: a step called `leave(...)`, HELD rather than run. It never appears in a beat's steps — `runList` lifts it out and keeps it — and when the scene unwinds for ANY reason (skip, X, a defeat, an error) the runner plays the final list last and in full. A `leave` list is what the scene ASSERTS about the world; it is deliberately not the same thing as 'the steps I happened to reach'.

WHICH IS WHY IT SITS AT THE TOP OF A BEAT, and that was the second, quieter half of this. `leave` is kept when `runList` REACHES it — and a skip stops `runList`. A finalizer at the bottom of a beat is therefore kept by exactly the readers who never needed it, and is missing for the one player who pressed skip. The first attempt put it at the end and fixed nothing at all: the flag stayed false and the beat re-armed. Every beat now opens with its finalizer.

THE GAME'S OWN OPENING IS A DIALOGUE BOX WAITING FOR A KEYPRESS. `storyAuto(false)` does not close it — it asks the running beat to let go, and a beat sitting on a line a child has not answered will not let go until somebody answers it. So this scenario plays the opening out for real, on Enter, and only then takes the controls away. A scenario that called `storyAuto(false)` over a live dialogue box and went on to measure things was measuring a beat nobody had finished.

steps.eval: (async()=>{await __DQ.storyAuto(false);for(let i=0;i<80&&__DQ.storyState().playing;i++)await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r,100));await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r,800));const S=await import('/src/engine/states.js');return JSON.stringify({auto:__DQ.heart().auto,playing:__DQ.storyState().playing,map:__DQ.state().map.id,stack:S.Scenes.stack()});})()

steps.note: 0. THE OPENING BEAT IS OVER, and it is in the history — so every count below starts at two, not zero. Reading 'two b1s in the history' as 'it played twice' is the reading this scenario exists to not make: the first one is the game's own opening, watched to its end, and the second is the pass under test.

steps.msg: the game's opening has been read to its end and the stage is clear — so what follows is this scenario's own beat and not the game's, and a `npc` reading means a real room

steps.note: 0. A CLEAN SLATE, and a way to get one back. Every pass below starts with no flags, or the later assertions are measuring the previous pass. `__DQ.beat().next` is the question the bug is really about: which beat the chapter would start NEXT.

steps.eval: (()=>{for(const k of Object.keys(__DQ.flags().flags||{}))__DQ.flag(k,null);__DQ.teleport('hollybank');return 'cleared, and in the cottage';})()

steps.msg: the flag is unset and the chapter is offering B1 — the state a skipped scene used to strand a child in, with the father standing in the room

steps.note: 1. SKIP IT. One call to skip, no key presses at all, no Enter, no mashing. The whole question is what the world looks like the moment the beat lets go.

steps.eval: (async()=>{__DQ.storyPlay('b1');await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r,800));const mid=!!__DQ.storyState().playing;const s=__DQ.storySkip();await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r,2000));return JSON.stringify({wasPlaying:mid,skip:s,ran:((__DQ.storyState().history||[]).slice(-1)[0]||{})});})()

steps.msg: one skip and the scene has let go of the stage

THE FIX, MEASURED. The beat was skipped at step 1 of 41, and the chapter still knows it happened: `ch1.awake` is the flag `blocks:` asks, and it is now set by the beat's `leave` list rather than by reaching step 26. Before the fix this was false, and stayed false.
and the chapter does NOT hand B1 back — the next beat it would start is B2, at the lane. Before the fix this stayed `b1` for ever, which is the second half of the bug: a beat that cannot be left.

the other thing the beat owes the world. A skip does not get to keep a father standing in a room he was told he had left — the `leave` list dismisses him for good, exactly as the line near the end of the beat does.
and it is not merely a flag: he is marked gone, so the cottage does not still have him in it the next time the boy walks in

steps.note: 2. THE SAME, THROUGH THE OTHER BUTTON. The X button and the skip button are one code path (`cancel` and `menu` both call Story.skip), so this presses the second of the two to be sure the fix is not sitting on one key. Note `__DQ.press('Escape')` is not a thing — the buttons are up/down/left/right/confirm/cancel/menu/run/map, and the one that opens the menu here is `menu`.

steps.eval: (async()=>{for(const k of Object.keys(__DQ.flags().flags||{}))__DQ.flag(k,null);__DQ.teleport('hollybank');for(let i=0;i<60&&__DQ.storyState().playing;i++)await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r,100));await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r,700));__DQ.storyPlay('b1');await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r,800));const k=__DQ.press('menu');await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r,2200));return JSON.stringify({key:k});})()

steps.msg: the same from the other button: one keypress out of the scene and the chapter has moved on

steps.note: 3. THE MIDDLE OF THE BEAT, not just its first line. A child who skips after the chest is opened is holding a wooden sword; one who skips after the crock has heard about the oatcake. Those are different states and every one of them has to leave the same world behind, so each pass plays the beat and skips a moment later — landing on a different step every time, which is what `ran`/`of` reports.

steps.eval: (async()=>{const out=[];for(const wait of [2400,5400,9000]){for(const k of Object.keys(__DQ.flags().flags||{}))__DQ.flag(k,null);__DQ.teleport('hollybank');for(let i=0;i<60&&__DQ.storyState().playing;i++)await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r,100));await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r,700));__DQ.storyPlay('b1');await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r,wait));__DQ.storySkip();await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r,2200));const h=((__DQ.storyState().history||[]).filter(e=>e.id==='b1').slice(-1)[0])||{};out.push({waited:wait,ran:h.ran,of:h.of,skipped:h.skipped,playing:!!__DQ.storyState().playing,awake:!!__DQ.flag('ch1.awake'),leftCottage:!!__DQ.flag('ch1.left_the_cottage'),gone:__DQ.npcsGone('hb-halvard')===true,next:((__DQ.beat()||{}).next||{}).id});}window.__mid=out;return JSON.stringify(out);})()

steps.msg: all three passes really were skipped rather than read out, and every one let go of the stage — otherwise the rows above prove nothing about the middle of the beat

THE FIX AT THREE POINTS IN THE MIDDLE. Every one of those left the world identical. The bug was never 'skip on the first line': it was that a scene's own steps are the wrong place to record what a scene has done, and every one of the twenty-seven beats recorded it that way.

steps.note: 4. AND THE BEAT STILL PLAYS ALL THE WAY THROUGH. A finalizer must not turn the beat into one nobody can read, and the steps it keeps must be the steps it always ran. No skip, real keys, and the flags the beat is supposed to end on.

steps.eval: (async()=>{for(const k of Object.keys(__DQ.flags().flags||{}))__DQ.flag(k,null);__DQ.teleport('hollybank');for(let i=0;i<60&&__DQ.storyState().playing;i++)await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r,100));await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r,700));__DQ.storyAuto(false);__DQ.storyPlay('b1');return 'playing b1 with no skip';})()

steps.msg: a beat that is READ still ends where it always ended — and the flags the skip now sets are the ones it was already setting, not new ones written for the skip
and it really did run to near the end: `ran` of `of` says the reader got all but the final step. A finalizer must not swallow the beat.

steps.note: 5. THE BUG AS A CHILD MET IT: skip, then stay in the room. Autoplay ON, standing in the cottage, and nobody walks back to Papa. This is the last thing to prove, because it is the sentence the bug was reported in.

steps.eval: (async()=>{for(const k of Object.keys(__DQ.flags().flags||{}))__DQ.flag(k,null);__DQ.teleport('hollybank');for(let i=0;i<60&&__DQ.storyState().playing;i++)await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r,100));await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r,700));__DQ.storyAuto(true);__DQ.storyPlay('b1');await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r,1200));__DQ.storySkip();await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r,2500));return JSON.stringify({playing:!!__DQ.storyState().playing,awake:!!__DQ.flag('ch1.awake'),canWalk:__DQ.state().input.blocked.length===0,papa:__DQ.npcs().filter(n=>/halvard/i.test(n.id)).map(n=>[n.id,n.hidden,n.gone])});})()

steps.msg: after a skip he is standing in his own front room with the controls back — a scene that lets go must hand the boy back to the field
and with autoplay ON, standing in the cottage does NOT open Papa's scene again. A beat that re-arms itself every frame is a beat a child has to walk away from twice.
